note: Re-judged 2026-10-31 by an independent auditor who authored none of the change. RFC text (rfc8669): "Similarly, if a recognized TLV appears more than once in a BGP Prefix-SID attribute while the specification only allows for a single occurrence, then all the occurrences of the TLV other than the first one SHALL be discarded and the Prefix-SID attribute will continue to be processed." The only edit to test/plugin/prefixsid-duplicate-tlv-relay.ci since the last judgement is f8f7628bdf, which adds a bgp-level filter { import { final accept; } export { final accept; } } with no filter refs, because RFC 8212 Section 3 now makes an EBGP direction with no explicit policy reject. No expect, reject, input or requirement-tag line changed. policy.ConcatChains keeps every peer-level ref and takes the final from the most specific configured level, so a peer-level chain still decides where one exists. An accepting final with no refs neither refuses nor rewrites a route: a withheld, stripped or discarded outcome the file asserts can still come only from the producer under test, and a delivered outcome is the eligibility the test was written under before RFC 8212; without the block the positives would fail for the wrong reason. What the unit proves is unchanged. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgements are in this file's git history.
